title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: usage reports for Copilot Search, connectors and agents in US Government clouds

reasons: published before the check existed: kept live with a notice while a corrected version is prepared

summary: Hold: automatic availability and included licensing are not established by the sources, so the no-cost rating is not justified. The privacy API exists, but the printed request omits its required Boolean value, and report-access automation is incorrectly described as undocumented.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; controls[2].note; Governance controls: third row
claims.claim: The government reports are on by default and appear automatically at rollout without an administrator enabling them.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot usage reports GCC automatically; Copilot usage reports GCC enable; 573170 reports default license. Read the roadmap, reporting options, usage overview and Search, Connectors and Agents report pages; none states this rollout default.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to unknown. Replace the third control's note with 'Microsoft has not documented a government-specific report switch or stated the rollout default as of November 2026.' Do not infer automatic enablement from the absence of a documented switch.

claims.claim: The new government reports are included in an existing licence.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft 365 Copilot Search connectors agents usage reports government license prerequisites pricing; Copilot usage reports government license reports. Read reporting options, usage overview and individual report pages; none names an included licence for this government release.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to unknown and retain a narrowly scoped note that licensing for the new government reporting release is not yet published. Do not treat membership of the admin center as proof of licence inclusion.

claims.claim: The cost rating can be none because these reports are in the admin center and no licence change is published.
claims.quote:
cost: "none"
No cost published. Reports are part of the Microsoft 365 admin center. Not yet published: any licence prerequisite.
cost: None. Reports are part of the Microsoft 365 admin center; no licence change is published.
claims.fix: Change cost to low and the rationale to 'Low. Admin time to review report access and adoption metrics; licensing for the government reporting release is not yet published.' The standard permits none only with explicit evidence of inclusion in licences already held.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Scope; Governance controls: first row
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot reports can be reached through Microsoft 365 admin center > Reports > Usage > Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
To view reports, go to Reports > Usage.
Select Microsoft Copilot > Readiness or Usage:

claims.claim: No API or automation is documented for controlling access to Copilot usage reports.
claims.quote:
Create a role assignment for the directory provider:
POST /roleManagement/directory/roleAssignments
claims.fix: Distinguish report navigation from access administration. Report-reader and AI Administrator access uses Microsoft Entra roles, which can be assigned through the documented Graph directory role-assignment API. Replace the absence with that general role-assignment mechanism, or remove this misleading access-control row and describe report navigation in prose.

claims.claim: The tenant-wide name-concealment setting is under Settings > Org settings > Services > Reports > Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.
claims.quote:
Select Org Settings.
On the Services tab, select Reports.
In the Reports panel, uncheck the checkbox next to Conceal user, group, and site names in all reports.

claims.claim: PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings { displayConcealedNames } is the documented request for changing report-name concealment.
claims.fix: The endpoint exists, but replace the body with valid JSON containing a Boolean, for example PATCH /beta/admin/reportSettings { "displayConcealedNames": true }. Explain true conceals names and false reveals them. Link to https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/adminreportsettings-update?view=graph-rest-beta rather than just the resource schema, and disclose that beta APIs are subject to change and unsupported for production applications. Do not blindly substitute v1.0: its deployment table excludes US Government L4 and L5.
